Overview

Drum roll

Every transcribed hit, one row per drum, with the tracked beat along the bottom. Opens on the 20 seconds around the most intense moment. Drag to pan, scroll or box-zoom, double-click to see the whole solo.

Over time

Density by instrument, loudness, tempo and novelty on one time axis. Dotted lines mark the 6 section boundaries found in the self-similarity analysis below.

Spectrogram

Mel spectrogram. Kick and floor tom sit at the bottom, snare and toms in the middle, cymbals across the top.

Instrument range

20 distinct GM drum notes in 7 families. Note entropy 2.93 bits (68% of the maximum for 20 notes); the three most-used notes take 66% of the hits. Snare 13%, hi-hat 11%, kick 20%, toms 15%, cymbals 38%.

Dynamics

Loudness distribution

Integrated -27.2 LUFS, loudness range 7.9 LU, crest factor 23.5 dB.

How hard each drum is hit

Per-hit level from the audio, for the families where it tracks velocity.

Snare: ghost notes to accents

Interquartile range 4.3 dB.

Dynamic contour

Median hit level per family over time.

Tempo consistency

Tracked pulse 120 BPM (10th to 90th percentile 113 to 124). Beat-to-beat variation 4.1% overall and 0.6% within 8-beat stretches; drift +2.68 BPM per minute. Which pulse level counts as "the beat" is ambiguous in a solo; the tracker picked this one, and the tempogram shows the others.

Tempogram

Periodicity strength at each tempo over time (dark = strong), with the tracked beat on top.

Beat-to-beat tempo

Rhythm and complexity

Time between strokes

Peaks line up with the subdivisions the drummer uses. Median 157 ms, entropy 3.57 bits, nPVI 35.9 (0 would be perfectly even spacing).

Position in the beat

Where in the beat each drum lands, one full turn per beat, with 16th positions at the quarters and triplets at the thirds.

Subdivisions

Each hit snapped to the nearest of 12 positions per tracked beat. Grid lock 0.29 (1 = every hit exactly on a 16th or triplet position, 0 = no relation to the grid). The lower the grid lock, the less these shares mean.

Stroke evenness

Inside steady runs (218 strokes), each stroke is compared with the midpoint of the strokes two either side, so swing counts as feel, not error. This ignores tempo drift entirely. Timing jitter 12.3 ms (9% of the stroke spacing). Measurement error was 1.6 ms on clean audio and is likely higher on a live recording.

Rhythmic vocabulary

Each beat reduced to a 12-step pattern. 42 distinct rhythms across 240 beats (82% of beats reuse an earlier one); 115 distinct once the choice of drum counts. Lempel-Ziv complexity 0.55 of a shuffled version of the same hits (1.0 = no structure).

Most-used one-beat rhythms

Structure

Each point compares two 2-second windows, relative to the solo's average (dark = alike). Squares on the diagonal are sections, and off-diagonal blocks are returns to earlier material. The three views show how it sounds, how it pulses, and what the transcription says was played. 6 sections, median 19 s, with peak intensity at 47% of the solo.

Phrasing

Stretches of playing separated by silences of at least 0.5 s: 15 phrases, median 0.5 s; rests take up 8% of the solo.

Playability

Hits closer than 30 ms are grouped as one stroke, and each stroke is counted by the hands and feet it needs. Counted in the solo's own MIDI: 0 groups need three or more hands (0.0 per minute), up to 2 at once.

Transcription accuracy

This solo's true notes are known, so the transcriber is scored on it directly. Onset F1 79% at a 50 ms tolerance with the drum family required to match (recall 72%, precision 88%).

Hits found, by family

Timing error

Median error 7.3 ms from the transcription alone, 1.4 ms after snapping each stroke to the sharpest nearby onset in the audio (83% within 5 ms). Every timing chart on this page uses refined times.

Does audio level track how hard a drum was hit?

The transcriber outputs every note at velocity 100, so dynamics come from the audio, from the peak energy in the instrument's frequency band right after each hit. Families with rho below 0.7 are left out of the dynamics charts above.

Which drums can the transcriber name?

Generated solos can use all 47 GM percussion notes, but the transcriber names fewer of them (about 20 in a typical solo), so the instrument range of a generated solo comes from its own MIDI.

Does the transcription follow the audio?

Transcribed density next to a transcription-free measure (mean spectral flux), per 2 s window. Correlation 0.70.
